newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended easier across the board. Spot March dropped by $3.30 to close at $308.20, while May gave up $3.10 to close at $307.10. In New York raw sugar futures ended lower but well off the day's lows after a round of fund buying recouped some of the market's early losses. March added 11 points to close 10.96 cents/lb, while may gave up 5 points to close at 11.05 cents/lb. The outer months declined by 3 to 5 points. Early weakness was largely attributed to the latest CFTC commitment of traders report valid through December 31 which showed speculators to be net long some 24,000 lots. Traders said speculators had since racked up 10,000 additional long positions as nearby March rallied last week to 10-week highs. The recent firm trend of world sugar prices is largely the result of fund buying and has no fundamental reasons.

THAILAND - 8.92 million tonnes of sugar cane had been crushed as of January 3, yielding 717,854 tonnes of sugar, tel quel. Yields rose to 86.52 kilograms of sugar per tonne of sugar cane and Commercial Cane Sugar (CCS), the available sugar in the cane, picked up to 10.69 per cent. Industry sources said that despite some initial delays, crushing seems to move quite smoothly and at a satisfactory pace. November elections and festivals had delayed the beginning of the crushing season by a few weeks.

AUSTRALIA - Sugar exports in October 1996 reached 601,911 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 815,421 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first five months of 1996/97 (June/October) up to 2.719 million tonnes against 2.560 million tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 4.177 million tonnes, down from a record high of 4.479 million tonnes attained in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in June/October 1996 were Canada with 539,482 tonnes raws against 391,897 tonnes, South Korea with 449,570 tonnes compared to 358,042 tonnes, Malaysia with 375,073 tonnes, down from 390,907 tonnes and Japan with 324,090 tonnes, down from 468,152 tonnes. Australia continues to be a sizeable white sugar supplier delivering a total of 109,768 tonnes in June/October 1996. The major countries of destination were New Zealand with 26,635 tonnes against nil, Indonesia with 20,132 tonnes compared to nil and Sri Lanka with 19,500 tonnes, up from 5,489 tonnes.

NORWAY - Sugar imports in November 1996 amounted to 17,605 tonnes, raw value, hardly changed from last year's 17,058 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first eleven months of 1996 (January/November) up to 174,519 tonnes against 159,759 tonnes in 1995. Total imports in 1995 were 173,712 tonnes, down from 192,368 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of origin in 1996 were Denmark with 100,037 tonnes whites against 105,898 tonnes, the UK with 40,545 tonnes, up from 34,603 tonnes and Sweden with 10,348 tonnes compared to 109 tonnes.

FIJI - According to ISO figures sugar exports in October 1996 reached 74,034 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 108,214 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first half of 1996/97 (May/October) up to 351,400 tonnes, slightly up on last year's 336,217 tonnes. Total exports in 1995 were 419,536 tonnes against 498,438 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in May/October 1996 were the European Union with 175,161 tonnes raws against 187,515 tonnes, Japan with 49,514 tonnes compared to 32,658 tonnes and Malaysia with 48,261 tonnes, down from 69,980 tonnes.
